newsitem.title: UK: BOE says examining alternatives to TARGET.
newsitem.headline: BOE says examining alternatives to TARGET.

text.p: The Bank of England said on Monday it is working on alternative approaches to TARGET, the cross-border settlement system for the euro, in case non-EMU members are offered limited access to intra-day liquidity.

European members have disagreed over who should get access to the European Central Bank's intraday credit facility following the start of European monetary union (EMU), with some countries arguing EMU "outs" be offered only limited access.

"Against this possibility we will be examining alternative approaches to ensure that banks in the UK remain able to make euro payments securely and efficiently," it said in its latest paper on City preparations for EMU. The Bank will examine a wide range of alternatives.

"One option could be arrangements for euro payments in the UK, in a real-time gross settlements context, which would not rely on access to intraday credit from the euro area," the Bank said in the third "Practical issues arising from the introduction of the Euro" paper.
It added that the full range of correspondent banking payment arrangements and end-of-day net settlement systems will continue to be available.
The Bank believes any attempt to offer EMU "outs" only limited access would be contrary to single market legislation and EU competition law.

"Some countries continue to feel that access by those member states which are not, or not yet, part of the euro area should be restricted because monetary policy concerns are raised... However, we do not believe that these concerns are justified," the paper said.
It added some progress had been made at the European Monetary Institute (EMI), the forerunner of the European Central Bank.
Some EU member, in particular France and Germany, oppose automatic equal access to intraday liquidity for EMU members and non-members.
The final deadline for a decision in spring 1998 when the ECB is set up, but Bank officials hope EMI will reach an agreement next year.
